newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AMP unit confirms fund raising.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP unit confirms fund raising.

text.p: AMP's PriorityOne Financial Services confirmed on Thursday it raised A$500 million late last year through a funding facility arranged by ABN AMRO.
It said the floating facility had been almost fully utilised and further significant funding arrrangements would be announced in due course.
PriorityOne managing director Tim Jones said the funds were needed to service the demand for PriorityOne's range of loan products.

"The need to seek further funds in the market demonstrates the continuing success of our loan business. It is a further recognition of the fact we are now a major player in the retail residential and investment property loan market," Jones said.
This was the second major fund raising activity undertaken by PriorityOne in less than a year.
Previously a A$425 million syndicated loan facility was arranged through ANZ Banking Group.
This was in addition to substantial AMP capital funding bringing PriorityOne's total funding to over A$1.0 billion.
Jones said the latest facility was finely priced reflecting the quality of assets in PriorityOne's business and its strong capital base.
"The keen pricing for this transaction is encouraging for PriorityOne's ongoing commitment to providing long term value to our customers," he added.
ABN AMRO Australia managing director Jerome Rowley said the bank recognised the strength and growth of financial insitutions and was keen to develop strong relationships in Australia.
"There is a natural affinity between ABN AMRO's global network and rapidly expanding, financially strong organisations such as PriorityOne," he added.
